_readme: TEMPLATE for eval/models.json, the LOCAL (gitignored) file that describes YOUR tiers.
Copy it: `npm run eval:setup` does so when models.json is missing, or copy it by hand.
Then: rename every <Placeholder> tier to the exact preset name your llama-server router
exposes (`llama-server --models-preset` / model.ini section names; also what `/v1/models` lists),
fill in the fields below, delete tiers you do not have, and run `npm run eval:setup` again
to generate eval/tiers/<Tier>.env. Keys starting with an underscore are comments; delete or keep them.
The loader rejects placeholder names (angle brackets) and unknown roles with a message that points here.
_languages: Natural languages, other than English, that your tiers should be tested in: lower-case codes, e.g. ["ro"].
Cases in tests/*.json that carry "lang": "<code>" run only when that code is listed here; English cases
always run. Leave [] to run English only. See README.md 'Adding a language' to add cases for another language.
_timeout_s: Per-request timeout in seconds for run_eval.py (promptfoo uses REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, default 600000). Long-context cases (24k-token prompts) and reasoning models need several minutes on consumer hardware.
_default_max_tokens: Answer budget for cases that set no max_tokens. Precedence: case max_tokens > tier max_tokens > this value.
_default_thinking_allowance: Extra tokens added to EVERY case's max_tokens for tiers whose chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking is true (see thinking_allowance below). Only used when a tier does not set its own.

models._comment: One entry per tier. The KEY is the tier name = the llama-server preset name; it also becomes eval/tiers/<Tier>.env, so use letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' only.

<ReasoningTier>._what: A model you run with thinking/reasoning enabled (e.g. a 'thinking' chat model). Example roles: everything but security.
_roles: Which suites this tier is measured on. Fixed vocabulary (anything else is rejected):
reasoning -> tests/reasoning.json (multi-step word problems, exact final answer)
coding    -> tests/coding.json (write/fix code; hidden unit tests run locally)
tools     -> tests/tools.json (multi-turn function calling with scripted tool results)
creative  -> tests/muse.json (creative writing, no refusals, rubric graded)
security  -> tests/sentinel.json (defensive security knowledge, no fabricated CVEs)
Suites with applies_to ["all"] (integrity, context, instruction) run for every tier regardless of roles.
<ReasoningTier>.notes: Free text for yourself: which GGUF/quant this preset loads, when you last changed it. Never read by the code.
_sampling: Sent verbatim in every request (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, repeat_penalty, ...).
Take the values from the model card's 'recommended sampling' / 'generation config' section on Hugging Face
(or generation_config.json in the original repo); thinking and non-thinking modes often have different values.
Do not tune them against the suites: the eval measures the preset as you actually run it.
_chat_template_kwargs: Passed as the top-level `chat_template_kwargs` request field, which llama-server feeds to the Jinja chat
template. Use it for the model's thinking toggle (the model card names the variable: enable_thinking for
Qwen-style templates, others differ) or any other template switch. {} sends nothing. A value here also
overrides the preset's own `reasoning` setting for the eval, without touching the server config.
_thinking_allowance: Only matters when chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking is true. On llama-server the chain of thought counts
toward max_tokens, so a case that asks for one word with max_tokens 32 would spend its whole budget thinking
and return an EMPTY answer (finish_reason=length). The harness adds this many tokens to every case's budget
for such tiers. Size it to the model's typical reasoning length (4096-8192 is common); too small truncates
answers, too large only costs time on runaway reasoning. Omit to use default_thinking_allowance.
<ReasoningTier>._max_tokens: Optional per-tier answer budget for cases without their own max_tokens (overrides default_max_tokens). Raise it for models that write long answers or when your context window allows; the thinking_allowance is added on top.

<AgentTier>._what: A fast instruct model you use for coding/agent work and everyday tasks, thinking off.
<AgentTier>._chat_template_kwargs: Empty: nothing is sent, the preset's own template defaults apply. Set {"enable_thinking": true} to measure the same preset with thinking (then also set thinking_allowance).

<SpecialistTier>._what: A small model with one job (here: security); a model with roles ["everyday"] or ["creative"] works the same way.

_base_url: Optional: add "base_url": "http://host:port" at the top level to override the server URL. By default the eval reads config/local-ai.json `server_url` and falls back to http://127.0.0.1:8080.
